as_read: Conflicting evidence with no clear benefit: one 9-man crossover is positive for endurance, two endurance trials and the placebo-controlled fatigue trial are not.
proposed_decision_text: Evidence on Eleutherococcus senticosus conflicts and shows no clear benefit. A randomized placebo-controlled trial in 96 adults with chronic fatigue reported that overall efficacy was not demonstrated (PMID 14971626). A trial in 20 distance runners reported that the data do not support an ergogenic effect (PMID 8778554), and a crossover in 9 cyclists found no difference in substrate use or 10-km time (PMID 11099371). A 144-person stress trial described any effect of adding it to stress training as negligible (PMID 23740477). One crossover in 9 recreationally trained men reported 23% longer endurance time at 800 mg/day (PMID 21793317). A 20-person trial in older adults found higher social functioning at 4 weeks that did not persist at 8 weeks (PMID 15207399). A 28-person trial reported surrogate autonomic changes (PMID 38525193), and a crossover in 50 women reported less lower-limb edema hours after powder (PMID 27333960). The fatigue and 800 and 1,200 mg trial abstracts do not state whether powder or extract was tested, so this reads the plant across preparations and doesn't say a powder failed.
